pr_body:
Fixes #28660
Fixes an admin api bug related to `user.LoginSource`
Fixed `/user/emails` response not identical to GitHub api

This PR unifies the user update methods. The goal is to keep the logic only at one place (having audit logs in mind). For example, do the password checks only in one method not everywhere a password is updated.

After that PR is merged, the user creation should be next.

issue_context.title: E-mail address change in LDAP creates separate address in gitea
issue_context.body:
### Description

When gitea is syncing users from LDAP, changing user's e-mail address in LDAP and syncing users to gitea (cron task) creates extra e-mail address for this user in gitea db (`email_address` table) but should only change existing e-mail address like in LDAP.

As result, all old user e-mail addresses are remembered in gitea and if other user is assigned in LDAP e-mail address that was already assinged in the past in LDAP (and was freed), say `test1@example.com`, syncing such user from LDAP to gitea throws an error
```
2023/12/30 15:56:50 .../ldap/source_sync.go:134:Sync() [E] SyncExternalUsers[ldap]: Error creating user test: e-mail already in use [email: test1@example.com]
```
because such freed e-mail address is still in use on gitea's side by previous user.

Consider updating gitea user's primary e-mail address only from LDAP mail attribute without creating separate entry in `email_address` table.

Related: https://github.com/go-gitea/gitea/issues/18603




### Gitea Version

1.21

### Can you reproduce the bug on the Gitea demo site?

No

review_comments: Currently you can't really edit the user emails as admin. We only can set the primary address. This method mimics this behaviour but I propose to remove the email field from the admin user forms in future in favor of extended email edit endpoints.

I think this method name is weird:
Why `some`, but you always initialize it?
What about `Must` or something like that?
Also, is `nil` a valid value? Sounds weird…

The terms `none` and `some` are usually used for an optional data type.
If `nil` a valid value depends on your usecase. If it is not, you should not use `Some`.

Which language?
I've never seen that notation.

https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Option_type
https://dotnet.github.io/dotNext/features/core/optional.html
https://developer.apple.com/documentation/swift/optional
https://github.com/nlkl/Optional
Interesting. TIL.

More thoughts from my opinion:

I can understand that many languages use "Some", but most languages using "Some" because they have "match" pattern like :

```
value = option.Match(
  some: ...
```

For languages like C++, which don't have "match" pattern , they never use "some", they only use "value": https://en.cppreference.com/w/cpp/utility/optional/optional

And Go is more C-style language, no match pattern.

To me, either is fine. I am pretty neutral.
This fixes #28660. If we decide this is not a bug but a breaking change, I will change this to `AddOrSetPrimaryEmailAddress` and make a separate PR.
I think this isn't expected behavior, so this shouldn't be considered as breaking
Same suggestion as above.
This method should return an email address without considering the user. The method below does what you are asking for.

?

2. Assume you accidentally enter whitespaces when creating a password. That can happen for example when copying from something (i.e. a password manager).  Whenever you try to login, you then need the whitespaces you didn't intend to have, thus you will never be able to use your own password as you don't know about the whitespaces.
This is only the password passed to HIBP. The password we use for the user is always untrimmed if chi binding does not auto trim string values.
